newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa backs Lesotho against police mutineers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa backs Lesotho against police mutineers.

text.p: The South African government on Saturday threw its weight behind the government of Lesotho Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle and said the kingdom should quell a 10-day-old police mutiny.
Eight officers last Thursday seized the police headquarters in the capital of Lesotho, a southern African mountain kingdom surrounded by and reliant on regional economic giant South Africa.
The mutiny in Maseru last Thursday has led to a national police strike, sparking concern among leaders of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) regional bloc.

"South Africa supports the government of Lesotho and together with its SADC partners cannot accept an unconstitutional challenge to the democratic order in Lesotho," South Africa's Department of Foreign Affairs said on Saturday.
"It is trusted that the government of Lesotho will take...appropriate measures necessary to restore orderly administration in the police services," the statement said.
The eight officers are resisting arrest for the alleged killing of three fellow officers in 1995. Up to 60 other policemen have joined them in occupying the police headquarters.
Church groups, non-governmental organisations and politicians are mediating but has so far been unsuccessful.
The rebels called a strike of Lesotho's 2,000 police officers from Thursday and by Friday most policemen were not at their posts, diplomats said.
The eight mutineers are demanding amnesty under Lesotho's Pardons Act, which stipulates that security force members may not be charged for crimes committed from 1993 to 1995.
